title: Policy-driven lifecycle for prompts, logs, and metrics with attestable export bundles
creator: Anika Patel
description: Problem: Customers building regulated workflows require deterministic, auditable lifecycles for request artifacts (prompts, model responses, request logs, and metrics). Current per-route TTLs are coarse and lack a single serialized artifact that proves correct retention/timestamping for audits. We need a policy-first retention model that supports composable rules (time-based, event-based, sample-based), soft vs hard delete semantics, and an attestable export bundle that can be handed to compliance teams or regulators.
outcome: Deliver a policy engine and orchestration that authoritatively applies retention rules across artifact categories and produces cryptographically-signed export packages (attested bundles) suitable for audits and legal requests. UX for policy authoring and a dry-run preview, runtime enforcement hooks, and an evidence assembly pipeline must be included.
milestones: M1: Policy DSL v0 (can express TTL, sampled retention, tenant overrides) - 2026-03-26
M2: Dry-run preview + retention simulator in Console - 2026-04-09
M3: Runtime enforcement APIs and soft-delete plumbing for prompts/responses - 2026-04-16
M4: Evidence assembler + signed export format (bundle spec) - 2026-04-23
M5: End-to-end QA, compliance review, and pilot with 2 tenants - 2026-04-30
tasks: Design retention policy DSL (operators: time, count, sample-rate, event-trigger, inherit)
Console: policy authoring UI with validation and preview sandbox
Retention simulator: show projected data volumes and sampled exports per policy
Runtime: implement policy evaluation hook in request router and storage tier
Storage: implement soft-delete markers and certifiable snapshot creation
Export: define signed bundle schema (manifest, provenance, hashes, signatures)
Docs: create admin guide and auditor-facing Evidence README
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL can express per-route and per-tenant rules for prompts, responses, logs, and derived metrics
Console shows a dry-run that accurately predicts retained vs purged counts for a representative 7-day dataset
Runtime honors soft-delete TTLs and exposes a purge job that can be invoked on demand
Export bundles include manifest with retention decisions, hash chain of included artifacts, and a service signature; auditors can verify integrity using public keys
End-to-end tests and a compliance review sign-off completed; pilot tenants confirm no data leakage and correct deletion timings
risks: Incorrect policy semantics could lead to under-retention for legal holds or over-retention causing regulatory exposure
Performance impact if snapshotting for attestable bundles is synchronous; may increase tail latency
Complex interactions between sampled retention (for low-value request logs) and metrics aggregation windows could break SLA for billing analytics
Key management for signing bundles requires coordination with Security/KMS and may add rollout friction
open_questions: Q1: Do we require per-tenant key pairs for signing export bundles or will a Redwoods-managed signing key suffice for initial pilot?
Q2: For sampled retention, should sampling be deterministic (stable by user id/hash) to allow reconstruction during audits?
Q3: How do we treat function/tool-call payloads that include customer-managed secrets — must they be redacted before snapshot?
Q4: What SLA do we guarantee for on-demand evidence assembly (e.g., 48 hours for a full attested export)?
notes: Compliance requested ability to sign bundles with tenant-specific audit metadata (requesting schema fields: tenant_id, policy_id, generated_at, retention_snapshot_hash)
See ENG-22678 for storage soft-delete implementation plan and impact matrix
